s.d: action with which a person touches her or his lips to another person (usually on the lips or cheek or hand) or to an object ► to show love or respect or devotion; also used when greeting and saying goodbye
state in which an object is located near enough to another object that they touch or rub together
exact meaning uncertain; possibly = action by which a person shows submission or accepts another's authority
s.g: to obey a comand; to be directed

s.d: exact meaning uncertain; possibly: = state in which a person is equipped with a weapon, especially a bow and arrows
s.g: to arm oneself; to be armed

s.d: causative action by which humans cause fuel such a firewood to start burning
s.g: to build a fire; to kindle a fire

s.d: causative action by which humans cause an object to start burning
literally: fire is kindled; hence: = process by which a deity experiences an extreme displeasure, ◄ as a fire that flares up
class of tools designed to attack and inflict bodily harm on someone else or to defend oneself against similar attacks from other people
building where weapons are stored
literally: day of weapons; hence: = time when an armed conflict takes place
s.g: day of battle; time of battle

s.d: substances with a fragrant aroma; ≈ regarded as valuable and therefore suitable as a gift

exact meaning unknown; possibly: = a grouping of large birds of prey with keen eyesight; ► unclean and therefore not to be eaten; ≈ associated with large size and great strength, ability to fly great distances at high speed; symbol of protection, metaphor for God, but also symbol for death in battle
s.g: large bird of prey; eagle; vulture

s.d: process by which a body of water or place that was formerly covered with moisture dries up, ◄ as a result of evaporation or draining; ► in the case of land, if this condition persists, sedentary life will become impossible
s.g: to become dry; to dry up

s.d: process by which objects containing liquid essential to their existence lose these liquids ◄ due to some external or internal cause
process by which a quality is gradually reduced in intensity, ◄ as a liquid that slowly dries up
written document; ► composed by government official and used to communicate instructions or information to other people
causative action by which humans cut a dead body in pieces with a knife, usually in order to cook it or to burn it on an altar as a sacrifce
a piece of a dead body that has been cut in pieces with a knife, usually in order to be cooked or to be burned on an altar

poetic term; = an open space connecting different places, ► used for travelling and transportation; ≈ often extended to denote our life as a journey from birth to death, and the totality of our activities during our lives
literally: to make level a path for (one's) anger; hence: = action by which deities give full vent to their anger
s.g: to give free course to (one's) anger

s.d: literally: path; hence: = pattern of behavior, with a primary focus on moral and ethical behavior, ◄ understood as a journey through life
literally: path; hence: = a visible proof that a moving object has passed a certain way
literally: path; hence: = the way to get from one place to another

poetic term; = a open space connecting different places, possibly slightly more narrow than a {L:road<SDBH:דֶּרֶךְ>} (see {S:02401801500032}), ► used for travelling and transportation; ≈ often extended to denote our life as a journey from birth to death, and the totality of our activities during our lives
literally: path; hence: = pattern of behavior, with a primary focus on moral and ethical behavior, ◄ understood as a journey through life
literally, "the ones given" or "the dedicated ones"; hence = persons who were responsbile for doing regular tasks in the Temple and for serving the priests
process by which water flows from heaven in the form of rain
causative process by which humans or deities cause a liquid or a quantity of small sized objects to flow from one place into another
literally: to pour our (one's) anger or wrath; hence: = action by which deities give full vent to their anger by administering punishment
literally: (an event) is poured out; hence: = process by which an event takes place with some degree of intensity ◄ like a liquid that is pouring out from a container
s.g: to be poured out > to happen with intensity

s.d: causative action by which humans or deities turn a solid substance into a liquid ◄ by exposing it to extreme heat
action by which humans transfer objects in their possession to other humans as a free gift or in exchange for something else
literally: to give (people) a covenant; hence: = action by which a deity initiates a covenant with a group of people
action by which humans force other humans to join a group of conscripted laborers
s.g: to force to join conscripted laborers

s.d: literally: to give (children); hence: causative action or progress by which humans or deities cause women to conceive and bear children
literally: to give (young); hence:= process by which animals generate offspring
literally: to give fire; hence: = causative process by which deities cause town or country to burn down
literally: to give (one's) love (to someone else); hence: = action by which humans have sexual relations with one another as a way to express their love
literally: to give lying down (to someone); hence: = action by which humans have sexual intercourse with other humans or animals; ≈ used for unlawful sexual relations only
literally: to give; hence: = causative action by which humans select one or more objects out of a larger quantity
literally: to give a tent peg (in a certain place); hence: = causative action or process by which deities cause humans to live in a place for an extended period of time
s.g: to give a stake; to give a stable home

s.d: literally: to give (someone) a place to live; hence: = action by which humans allow other humans to stay in a certain location for a certain amount of time
literally: to give (an event to someone); hence: = causative action or process by which humans or deities cause (other) humans to engage with an event
literally: to give as law; hence: = causative action by which people in a position of authority establish something as law
literally: to give (a quality to others); hence: = action by which humans waste one of their qualities by spending it on an unworthy goal
s.g: to give away; to spend; to waste

s.d: literally: to give; hence: = causative action by which deities put something in place that was not there before
literally: to give (a product); hence: = process by which nature produces products such as plants, trees, water, crops, etc.
literally: to give (someone) a complete heart; hence: = causative action or process by which which deities cause humans to be fully committed to a deity or a certain activity
meaning unsure; literally: to give eye; hence, possibly: = process by which an object is attractive to look at
literally: to give splendor; hence: = state in which a town shows that it is worthy of honor and respect ◄ because of its beauty, power, or fame
literally: to give (an event); hence: = causative action or process by which humans or deities cause an event to take place
s.g: to give; to send; to show

s.d: literally: to give (what someone desires); hence: = causative action by which humans or deities make happen what (other) humans request or desire
literally: to give (one's voice or a sound); hence: = action by which humans, deities, and animals produce sounds using their voice or a musical instrument
s.g: to utter (one's) voice; to sound (one's) voice; to play (an instrument)

s.d: literally: to give; hence: = causative action by which humans or deities place an object in someone else's hands or custody, but which does not involve a transfer of ownership
s.g: to give; to hand; to deliver

s.d: literally: to give in (someone's) hands; hence: = causative action by which humans or deities place an object in someone else's hands or custody, but which does not involve a transfer of ownership
s.g: to give; to hand; to deliver

s.d: literally: to give on (someone's) hands; hence: = causative action by which humans place an object in someone else's hands, but which does not involve a transfer of ownership
s.g: to give; to hand; to deliver

s.d: literally: to give (someone or something) in the hands (of others); hence: = causative action by which humans or deities allow (other) humans, animals, plants, lands, towns to fall under the authority of others
s.g: to give in the hands (of someone)

s.d: literally: to give (someone or something to others); hence: = causative action by which humans or deities allow (other) humans or animals to fall under the authority of others
literally: to give (a task); hence: = causative action by which humans assign certain responsibilities to other humans or deities
s.g: to give in (someone's) hand; to make responsible for (a certain task)

s.d: literally: to give; hence: = causative action by which humans set apart objects for a particular purpose or activity relating to the service of a deity
literally: to give (information); hence: = causative action by which humans or deities pass on information to others
literally: to give (a time); hence: = causative action by which humans or deities inform (other) humans about the time a certain activity will take place
literally: to give (a quality to someone); hence: = action by which humans acknowledge that a deity has a certain quality
literally: to give (as wife); hence: = action by which humans in authority, like a fathers, relatives, or even slave owners, allow another person to marry their daughter or female slave
literally: to give place; hence: = action by which humans retreat to give space to other humans
literally: to give a lamp; hence: = causative action by which a deity grants a ruler to be succeeded by a family member
s.g: to give a lamp; to give a successor

s.d: literally: to give (someone); hence: = action by which humans with some level of authority release a person in their custody or under their responsibility
s.g: to hand over; to give up; to release

s.d: literally: to give respect; hence: = action by which humans treat other humans with honor and respect
exact meaning unsure; literally, possibly: to give slander; hence: = action by which humans speak bad about alleged faults they find with other humans
literally: to give (people); hence: = action by which deities provide people to fulfill a certain role
literally: to give (people) a fence; hence: = causative process or action by which deities keep  humans from harm as by surrounding them with a protective fence
literally: to give (someone) a shield of salvation; hence: = action by which deities provide protection to humans and give them victory in battle
s.g: to give a shield of salvation; to provide safety and victory

s.d: literally: to grant a remnant; hence: = causative action by which a deity allows humans to survive after a fatal incident
literally: to give; hence: = causative action by which humans or deities place an object in a certain location
s.g: to place; to put; to lay

s.d: literally: to put fear in (someone's) heart; hence: = causative action or process by which deities cause humans to experience {L:fear<SDBH:יִרְאָה>}
literally: to make (something a certain quality); hence: = causative process or action by which deities cause humans or objects to have a certain quality
s.g: to make (something to have a certain quality)

s.d: literally: to place (one's) way on (one's own) head; hence: = action by which humans bring guilt upon themselves by their actions
literally: to place bloodshed of war on (one's) girdle; hence: = action by which humans bring guilt upon themselves by shedding blood during a time of peace
s.g: to be guilty of bloodshed during a time of peace

s.d: literally: to place (sins on an animal); hence: = causative action by which humans transfer the responsibility for their sinful actions to an animal
literally: to place (someone's deeds) on (that person); hence: = action by which deities punish humans (for their evil deeds)
s.g: to punish; to requite; to repay

s.d: literally: to place (guilt) on (someone else's) head; hence: = causative action by which deities hold humans responsible for their actions
literally: to place (innocent blood); hence: = causative action by which deities hold humans responsible for the death of someone else while they are innocent
literally: to place (an obligation on oneself); hence: = action by which humans take the responsibility to carry out a certain activity
literally: to place (an obligation on someone else); hence: = causative action by which humans cause other humans take the responsibility to carry out a certain transaction
literally: to place (one's) hand (on people); hence: = action by which a deity punishes a nation in order to achieve a certain purpose
s.g: to lay (one's) hand (on someone); to punish

s.d: literally: to make (something) like (something else); hence: = causative action or process by which humans or deities cause (other) humans or objects to take on some of the characteristics of (other) humans or objects
literally: to place (someone) on (someone else's) throne; hence: = causative action by which deities place humans in a position of royal authority over a group of people
s.g: to set (someone) on the throne; to make (someone) king

s.d: literally: to place a key on (someone's) shoulder; hence: = causative action by which humans in a position of authority give a certain amount of authority to other humans
s.g: to place a key on (someone's) shoulder > to give (someone) authority

s.d: literally: to place (one's) dwelling (somewhere); hence: = action by which humans or deities make their dwelling in a certain location

literally: to place (one's) spirit on (someone else); = causative action by which deities cause humans engage with part of the divine which can manifest itself as an invisible force equipping humans with wisdom, skill, and strength for specific tasks, giving direction to the people of God and, in specific cases, misdirection to those who oppose him
s.g: to put a spirit (in or on someone)

s.d: literally: to place an assembly; hence: = causative action by which humans in authority call together a group of people for a certain purpose
literally: to place in high places; hence: = caustave action or process by which humans are placed in positions with high status
s.g: to put in high places; to promote

s.d: literally: to place (someone's) throne above the throne (of others); hence: = causative action by which someone in authority gives one king a higher position than others
s.g: to give (a king) a throne above the throne (of others); to honor a king above (other kings)

s.d: literally: to place (something) to be (something else); hence: = causative action or process by which humans or deities turn objects into something else
literally: to place (an incision or mark one's own body); hence: = action by which humans use a sharp object to make incisions or marks on their body
literally: to place an injury (on someone); hence: = causative action by which people wound or disfigure someone else's body
literally: to place words in (someone's) mouth; hence: = causative action or process by which deities help humans know what to say
literally: to place lots; hence: = causative action by which humans put marks on a number of objects in order to be able to select one by throwing lots
literally: to place (someone in a certain position); hence: = causative action by which humans or deities give (other) humans a certain position or role
literally: to place a yoke (on someone else); causative action by which humans in authority force other humans to serve them
s.g: to lay a yoke (on someone); to lay a burden (on someone)

s.d: literally: to give (someone) a song in the night; hence: = causative action by which a deity gives humans a reason to sing for joy during difficult times
s.g: to give songs in the night

s.d: literally: to give (someone) a new song in (their) mouth; hence: = causative action by which a deity gives humans a reason to sing for joy after a time of trouble
s.g: to give a new song in (one's) mouth; to teach (someone) to sing again

s.d: literally: to place (one's) face (in a certain direction); hence: = action by which humans turn their face in a certain direction
literally: to turn (someone else's) face (in a certain direction); hence: causative action by which humans cause animals to look into a certain direction
s.g: to turn (someone's) face (in a certain direction)

s.d: literally: to place (one's) face (in a certain direction); hence: = action by which humans or deities direct their attention to a group of (other) humans, either with positive or negative intentions
literally: to place (something) towards (one's own) heart; hence: = action by which humans make a conscious effort to understand a certain matter
s.g: to take (someting) to heart; to think about; to consider

s.d: literally: to place (something) towards (someone else's) heart; hence: = causative action or process which deities cause humans to make a conscious effort to understand a certain matter
s.g: to put in (someone's mind); to make (someone) think about (something)

s.d: literally: to place (something) in (someone else's) heart; hence: = causative action or process which deities cause humans to make a conscious effort to understand a certain matter
s.g: to put in (someone's mind); to make (someone) think about (something)

s.d: literally: to place (someone or something) as (someone or something); hence: = state in which humans mistake a person or object for someone or something else

literally: to place (something) before (someone); hence: = causative action by which a deity puts forward an object or condition for humans to decide as to whether they will take control of it or engage with it
s.g: to set before; to propose; to offer

s.d: literally: to place (someone) as (someone else); hence: = state in which humans mistake a person for someone else
literally: to place a trap; hence: = process by which a condition leads to a dangerous situation
s.g: to lay a snare; to bring on danger

s.d: literally: to place (one's) law in the innermost parts (of people); hence: = causative action or process by which deities give humans a willing disposition to carry out God's laws
s.g: to put (one's) law in (someone else's) innermost being; to make obedient to (one's) law

s.d: literally: to place (wisdom or skill) in (someone's) heart; hence: = causative action or process by which deities give make humans wise or skilled
s.g: to put wisdom in (someone's) mind; to make (someone) wise

s.d: literally: to give a word; hence: = action by which deities give instruction to humans
literally: to give (someone) opening of mouth; hence: = causative action or process by which deities give humans to power and ability to speak out
s.g: to give (someone) the power to speak

s.d: literally: to give confession; hence: = action by which humans publicly admit their own shortcomings before God, or the shortcomings of the people they represent
literally: to give (one's) hand; hence: = action by which humans stretch out their arm
literally: to give (someone) a place (to sit); hence: = causative action by which humans in authority assign (other) humans a place to sit in an assembly
s.g: to give a place (to sit); to assign a place (to sit)

s.d: literally: to stretch out (one's) hand; hence: = action by which humans make a solemn statement often calling on a higher power to confirm that what is said is true or to punish the speaker if it turns out not to be true
s.g: to stretch out (one's) hand; to take an oath; to pledge allegiance

s.d: literally: to give (one's) heart (on an activity); hence: = action by which humans decide wholeheartedly to study a certain condition or engage in a certain activity
literally: to give (one's) heart; hence: = action by which humans pay attention to other humans and what they do or say
literally: to give (someone) a heart (in order to do something); hence: = causative action or process by which deities cause humans to decide wholeheartedly to carry out a certain activity
literally: to give someone's neck; hence: = causative action or process by which deities cause humans to turn around to flee
literally: to give (up); hence: = action by which humans or deities suspend their commitment to (other) humans or objects under their care, either temporarily or permanently
s.g: to give up; to hand over

s.d: literally: to give (one's) neck; hence: = action by which humans turn around as an attitude denoting rejection
literally: to give a stubborn shoulder; = action by which humans show themselves to be stubborn and unwilling to yield
s.g: to turn a stubborn shoulder; to refuse to obey

s.d: literally: to give a blessing; hence: = action by which humans utter a benediction
literally: to give (someone permission to do something); hence: = state in which humans or deities are willing to permit others to carry out a certain activity
s.g: to allow; to permit; to let

s.d: literally: to give (one's body to a smiter); hence: = action by which humans willingly offer part of their body to people who want to strike it
literally: to give (people) a heart; hence: = causative action or process by which deities give humans a willing disposition, symbolized by a new heart
s.g: to give a (new) heart; to give an obedient heart; to make obedient

s.d: literally: who will give ...?; hence: = expression denoting a wish for something to happen

man; ► father of {L:Jehudi<SDBH:יְהוּדִי>}, official, time of king {L:Jehoiakim<SDBH:יְהֹויָקִים>}

literally: to break down (someone's) path; hence: = causative action by which human make someone else's life impossible as if it were a road that had been made impassable
causative action by which someone removes an object with force from the place to which it was attached
causative action by which humans destroy a construction by removing all its parts
s.g: to tear down; to pull down; to break down

s.d: literally: to tear down; hence: = causative action by which deities bring destruction and hardship to individuals and kingdoms
s.g: to tear down; to bring destruction; to cause suffering

s.d: causative action by which an object is removed from its place with some force
s.g: to pull off; to tear off; to wrench off; to tear out; to remove; to drag away

s.d: causative action by which humans exert force on an object with the purpose of tearing it or breaking it in two
s.g: to tear; to break; to snap

s.d: causative action by which humans cause other humans to move away from a certain place
exact meaning unsure: = infection of the skin; ► causing uncleanness
literally: to loosen the cords of the yoke; hence: = action by which humans stop oppressing other people
s.g: to loosen the cords of the yoke > to stop oppressing other people

s.d: literally: to release (one's) hand; = action by which a deity lets go of whatever restrains him from acting in a certain way
s.g: to give one's hand free play

s.d: action by which humans or deities give freedom to (other) humans that were held in bondage
literally, possibly: to loosen (somone's) way blameless; hence: = causative action by which deities help humans to live a blameless life
action by which certain insects move by jumping from one place to the other
s.g: to jump; to leap; to hop

s.d: literally: (one's) heart leaps from its place; hence: = state in which humans experience a state of strong fear, which results in one's heart beating wildly
literally: to cause (people) to leap; hence: = causative action by which deities cause humans to experience a state of extreme fear which makes their bodies shake
causative action by which someone removes all leaves from the branches of a tree
sodium carbonate ► used as a dye, medicament, and cleansing agent (AYBC)
causative action by which a plant or pole is pulled out of the ground; ≈ associated with destruction and exile
literally: to uproot; hence: = causative action by which a town or land is destroyed, ◄ like a plant pulled out of the ground
literally: to be uprooted; hence: = process by which a body of water ceases to flow and vanishes
literally: to be uprooted; hence: = process by which a state of affairs comes to a violent end
s.g: to be uprooted > come to an end

s.d: literally: to uproot; hence: = causative action by which deities cause people to leave their land, ◄ like a plant pulled out of the ground
unit of dry measure equivalent to 7.3 liters or 7 quarts; 3 seahs make up 1 {L:ephah<SDBH:אֵיפָה>}
covering for the foot and leg ◄ made of leather ► used by soldiers ≈ associated with aggression
to walk heavily and firmly; ≈ associated with marching soldiers
state in which a condition has a specific degree of intensity
meaning unsure; possibly: = state of opposition or hostility between two or more persons
meaning unsure; possibly: = state of fierce anger
meaning unsure; possibly: = causative action by which humans are forced to live their dwelling-place
action by which humans consume alcoholic beverages in large quantities, ► which results in drunkenness and other forms of loose behavior, ≈ and is generally regarded as foolish and unacceptable
s.g: to drink in excess; to be a drunkard

s.d: a person who has the habit of consuming alcoholic beverages in large quantities ► which results in drunkenness and other forms of loose behavior; ≈ regarded as foolish and unacceptable
man; ◄ son of {L:Cush<SDBH:כּוּשׁ>}; descendant of {L:Ham<SDBH:חָם>} ► founder of a nation bearing the same name
ethnic group ◄ founded by Seba, son of {L:Cush<SDBH:כּוּשׁ>}, regarded as a descendant of {L:Ham<SDBH:חָם>}
kind of alcoholic beverage
member of the ethnic group ◄ founded by {L:Seba<SDBH:סְבָא>}; ≈ known as people tall of stature
process by which a door is attached to a wall by means of a {L:hinge<SDBH:צִיר>}, or a contraption with a similar function, which allows it to pivot
action by which humans, supernatural beings, forces of nature, or other objects face a direction different from the one they were facing before
literally, possibly, to turn on (someone's) life; hence: = state in which someone is held responsible for the death of someone else
literally: to turn (a situation); hence: = causative action by which humans cause a certain condition or process to be different
literally: to turn; hence: = process by which an object becomes significantly different
literally: to turn (one's) face (from someone); hence: = action by which humans or deities refrain from engaging in an activity involving another party
